mechanism: literal-substring-replace, applied to every byte of the file, both forms, order-independent, idempotent
patternEncoding: the slash-form pattern is written with \u002f JSON escapes so that this rule file, which is itself tracked, does not carry in its own bytes the literal home-path substring that the privacy-lint-user-paths claim refuses; a JSON parser decodes the escapes before matching, so the pattern applied is the unescaped literal string and nothing about the transformation changes
appliesTo: every byte of every file enumerated in the transformation's own record (INTEGRITY.md § Path transformation — declared), matched and replaced as literal strings, never a regex or a glob
recompute: new_bytes = bytes(original_file) with every literal occurrence of each decoded patterns[].pattern replaced by its replacement, nothing else changed, no reordering, no line-ending change, no encoding change; the two patterns share no byte sequence, so the order of application does not affect the result
idempotence: the replacement <LOCAL_ROOT> contains neither decoded pattern, therefore a second application of recompute to an already-transformed file is a no-op and yields identical bytes; a partially transformed input, some occurrences already rewritten and some not, converges to the same output as a never-transformed input carrying the same occurrences
whyTwoForms: the operator home path appears in Claude Code session evidence in two encodings: the filesystem form, as it occurs in cwd and transcript_path values, and the dash-flattened form -Users-pietrofalco, as it occurs in Claude Code's per-project state directory names under ~/.claude/projects/. path-transform/v1 declared only the slash form; the remote side of this merge carries 396 occurrences of the dash form and zero of the slash form, so v1 was vacuous against that evidence and is superseded here rather than amended
reason: privacy-lint-user-paths (harness-pack .verity/claims.json) refuses a tracked file carrying a literal operator home path; the evidence under runs/THR-SUBAGENT/20260813T194853Z/ is Claude Code session transcripts and derived files that recorded the executing session's own cwd, transcript_path and project-state directory, which is the local operator home path, not evidentiary content the transformation destroys — the path is incidental to what each fixture measures, never the subject of it
declares: a re-pin of a tracked blob's digest is evidence of this transformation, not of undetected tampering, exactly when this rule file is present alongside the re-pin, its own sha256 matches the digest the re-pin cites, and re-running recompute above against the pre-transform bytes reproduces the declared post-transform sha256 — a re-pin found without this rule, or against a rule whose digest does not match, is undeclared and MUST be treated as unverified content drift, not as this transformation
